The preliminary unloaded-current allocations total 1.791 mA, but actual compliance remains UNKNOWN until programming/control current, leakage, and datasheet conditions are verified; this turn does not claim hardware or downstream-stage validation.

# Protected USB-C 500 mA Power Breakout Specification

Status: requirements seed for an independent, reviewable prototype. No prototype has been manufactured or physically tested. Candidate parts and estimates below are not approved selections or verified hardware results.

## Provenance and interpretation

REQUIRED identifies the original product brief. ASSUMED identifies a proposed default or preliminary allocation not supplied as a requirement. SUPPLIED RESEARCH identifies additional public research embedded in the 2026-10-08 brief; this stage has not independently browsed those sources, verified prices, or run local library/pin/footprint checks. Proposed design choices require later confirmation. Every decision includes its rationale. Requirements and assumptions are recorded alongside their machine-readable constraint records.

The prior searches returned no existing design-document content. The validated proposal established an OpenSpec workspace, so this change seeds per-capability scenarios as well as this specification. No KiCad source is modified in this requirements stage.

## Budgets

The following is the complete preliminary unloaded-current accounting framework, not a claim of verified compliance. All entries below are VBUS input-current allocations in mA. Supplied component research has not been independently inspected in this stage. The actual total remains UNKNOWN until conditions and leakage bounds are established. Do not accept the candidate merely because its nominal LED and IC currents appear small.

Source conditions: attached nominal-5 V USB-C source, input within 4.75-5.25 V, both external output connectors unloaded, switch enabled and settled, LED illuminated, no fault and no other power source/backfeed. Check both range endpoints and any internal maxima across temperature/tolerances. CC Rd current is supplied on CC by the source and is accounted separately from this board's VBUS-input current; it is not silently omitted from the USB attachment design.

| Accounting bin | Preliminary ceiling (mA) | Evidence status |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Protected-rail LED and 10 kohm 1% resistor | 0.531 | Conservative resistor calculation; selected LED and visibility unverified |
| Enabled switch internal supply/control | 0.160 | Supplied research; conditions and current-definition boundary unverified |
| Additional ILIM/control current excluded from supply-current figure | 1.000 | ASSUMED allocation; actual upper bound unknown |
| External pull-ups/bias | 0 | ASSUMED intentionally absent; topology confirmation pending |
| Input/output capacitor leakage | 0.050 | ASSUMED allocation; bounds unknown |
| PCB/connector/other fitted protection leakage | 0.050 | ASSUMED allocation; inventory and bounds unknown |
| Other VBUS-fed loads | 0 | ASSUMED none; revisit after component selection |
| Allocation sum | 1.791 | Conditional planning total only |
| Unallocated distance to exclusive 2 mA boundary | 0.209 | Headroom, not a fitted load or measured margin |

Resolve the supply-current definition before summing real device currents: if ILIM or EN current is already included in the IC figure, charge it once to that bin; otherwise derive and include its separate worst-case contribution. If the candidate cannot meet the whole-board requirement after legitimate reallocation, reject the candidate rather than relaxing the brief.

- **power.input_voltage_v**: REQUIRED: nominal 5 V USB-C VBUS input; guaranteed design operating range must cover 4.75 to 5.25 V. No guaranteed operation or sustained-short performance at 6 V is required.
  - Rationale: The operating range is distinct from a component absolute-maximum stress rating.
- **power.external_continuous_load_ma**: REQUIRED: deliver up to and including 500 mA TOTAL normal continuous external load across the two parallel outputs; either connector must carry the full 500 mA when used alone. The LED and protection/control currents are additional input demand, not part of that external-load allowance.
  - Rationale: Parallel connectors share one load budget and one protection block.
- **power.unloaded_vbus_current_ma**: REQUIRED: total steady-state unloaded VBUS input current is strictly LESS THAN 2 mA, with both external outputs open and the protection enabled. The numeric boundary 2 is exclusive. Count LED, enabled protection/control, programming and pull-up currents not already included in another entry, all leakage, and every other fitted VBUS-fed load. Demonstrate the worst case throughout 4.75-5.25 V and the ASSUMED ambient range, including component tolerances. Startup and fault current are separate operating cases, not disguised as unloaded steady-state current.
  - Rationale: An incomplete or nominal-only sum cannot establish compliance.
- **budget.led_current_ma**: ASSUMED design candidate/allocation: a protected-rail LED with a 10 kohm, 1% series resistor has a conservative current ceiling of 0.531 mA at 5.25 V, using Rmin = 9900 ohm and the deliberately conservative bound Vf >= 0 V: 5.25/9900 = 0.530304 mA, rounded upward. No minimum brightness or actual LED Vf has yet been verified.
  - Rationale: This ceiling avoids inventing an LED forward-voltage specification; visibility still needs checking.
- **budget.enabled_switch_current_ma**: ASSUMED preliminary allocation: 0.160 mA for enabled switch supply/control current. SUPPLIED RESEARCH reports a 160 microampere maximum for MIC2544-2YM under datasheet conditions; the exact conditions, full operating-range coverage, and inclusion or exclusion of ILIM and other terminal currents remain unverified.
  - Rationale: The reported value is a starting evidence lead, not an independently confirmed whole-board bound.
- **budget.programming_control_extra_ma**: ASSUMED preliminary allocation: at most 1.000 mA of additional VBUS input current for ILIM programming and control paths EXCLUDED from the preceding supply-current definition. The actual upper bound is UNKNOWN. If the datasheet includes a contribution in supply current, count it there only and do not also count it here.
  - Rationale: An explicit unresolved allocation exposes the programming-current risk without double counting or claiming it is satisfied.
- **budget.external_pullup_current_ma**: ASSUMED preliminary allocation: 0 mA for external pull-ups because the proposed always-enabled, unmonitored implementation fits no FLG pull-up and no VBUS-fed EN bias resistor. This zero applies only if that topology is confirmed electrically suitable for the exact variant. Any later fitted bias or pull-up must receive its own worst-case current entry.
  - Rationale: An unused open-drain status signal does not need a pull-up merely to create a logic level nobody reads.
- **budget.capacitor_leakage_ma**: ASSUMED preliminary allocation: input and output capacitor leakage combined must be at most 0.050 mA at worst-case voltage and temperature. Actual component leakage bounds have not been obtained.
  - Rationale: Decoupling leakage belongs in the unloaded input-current total.
- **budget.board_connector_protection_leakage_ma**: ASSUMED preliminary allocation: at most 0.050 mA combined for connector/PCB insulation leakage and any other fitted VBUS-connected protection-device leakage not already included above. Actual bounds and any added-device list remain unverified.
  - Rationale: Leakage paths and future protection additions must not disappear from the current accounting.
- **budget.other_vbus_loads_ma**: ASSUMED preliminary allocation: 0 mA for other VBUS-fed loads because none are currently proposed. This is an inventory assumption, not a measured zero. Adding any load requires updating the budget and its constraint record.
  - Rationale: The design has no processor, firmware, converter, or other planned auxiliary consumer.
- **budget.unloaded_planning_total_ma**: ASSUMED allocation sum: 0.531 + 0.160 + 1.000 + 0 + 0.050 + 0.050 + 0 = 1.791 mA, leaving 0.209 mA below the exclusive 2 mA boundary. This is a planning allocation, NOT a verified worst-case device-current sum. The actual worst-case total is UNKNOWN until every contribution has a justified bound and non-overlapping accounting. Reallocations require documentation and must preserve the strictly below 2 mA requirement.
  - Rationale: An explicit conditional total and unallocated remainder keep the target useful without fabricating compliance.
- **cost.component_bom_usd_q100**: REQUIRED target: fitted component BOM strictly below USD 8 per board at quantity 100, including USB-C input, both output connectors, active protection, LED, and every supporting component; exclude PCB fabrication, assembly, shipping, and tax. The numeric boundary 8 is exclusive. Use dated price evidence or explicitly uncertain estimates. No complete BOM or verified cost total exists at this stage.
  - Rationale: The target applies to the whole populated component set rather than just the principal IC.
- **mechanical.envelope_mm**: REQUIRED target board envelope no larger than 40 x 30 mm. ASSUMED initial rectangular envelope: 40 x 30 mm, subject to exact connector fit and accessible assembly.
  - Rationale: The initial outline uses the stated size allowance without inventing an enclosure constraint.

## Electrical requirements and proposed implementation

- **product.scope**: REQUIRED: this is a NEW independent protected USB-C 500 mA power-breakout prototype test input, not a revision of the previous 3 A / USD 3 design. It is a sink-side power input with no USB data, no USB-PD negotiation, and no voltage conversion.
  - Rationale: Explicit scope prevents accidental inheritance of the earlier load and cost assumptions.
- **usb.cc_termination**: REQUIRED: fit separate 5.1 kohm Rd resistors from CC1 to GND and from CC2 to GND; never join CC1 and CC2. ASSUMED resistor tolerance: 1%. Rd enables attachment; it does not negotiate a current entitlement or enforce the source advertised-current limit.
  - Rationale: Separate Rd supports sink attachment in either connector orientation without claiming current negotiation.
- **usb.source_cable_condition**: REQUIRED operating condition: full-load use requires a known-capable source and cable suitable for 500 mA external load PLUS board overhead and startup demand. This power-only design does not establish advertised-current entitlement through Rd alone. Source/cable and protection interactions during inrush/overload require validation.
  - Rationale: A nominal 500 mA external load does not imply exactly 500 mA drawn from the source.
- **outputs.connectors_polarity**: REQUIRED: one 2-pin 3.5 mm screw terminal and one 2x2 2.54 mm header, connected in parallel downstream of common protection. ASSUMED proposed pin assignment: screw terminal pin 1 = +5V_PROTECTED, pin 2 = GND; header pins 1 and 3 = +5V_PROTECTED, pins 2 and 4 = GND. Clearly mark polarity and pin 1 on the board and document the actual view/orientation. Confirm these proposals against actual symbol pins, footprint pad numbers, and the selected connector drawings before wiring.
  - Rationale: A repeated power/ground pair is easy to document, but physical orientation must come from verified parts.
- **power.output_voltage_contract**: ASSUMED: output voltage tracks input minus protection, connector, and copper voltage drops; no tighter regulated output-voltage minimum is specified. Calculate worst-case loaded drop at the minimum input and include it in later review.
  - Rationale: There is no voltage converter or regulator, so exact 5 V at the output cannot be promised.
- **protection.common_active_topology**: REQUIRED: a common active high-side short-circuit protection block precedes BOTH external outputs and the visible power LED. A passive fuse is not an acceptable substitute. Explain fault-control and recovery using exact-device evidence; do not claim tested fault safety.
  - Rationale: One protected rail ensures neither connector nor the indicator bypasses the active protection.
- **protection.provisional_control**: ASSUMED candidate implementation: MIC2544-2YM always enabled using its reported active-low EN tied to GND, FLG intentionally unconnected without a pull-up, and NC left unconnected; connect both reported OUT pins. These are proposals pending exact-variant datasheet and actual-library pin confirmation. No MCU is introduced to operate or observe the switch.
  - Rationale: Always-on protection satisfies the power-breakout function without spending current on unused status circuitry.
- **indicator.visibility**: REQUIRED: a visible power LED on +5V_PROTECTED. ASSUMED starting choice: efficient red indicator with the budgeted 10 kohm 1% resistor; select its actual part and check visibility at minimum input and expected viewing conditions.
  - Rationale: The current ceiling alone does not establish acceptable brightness.
- **protection.decoupling_candidates**: SUPPLIED RESEARCH: input decoupling guidance is 0.1-1 microfarad near the switch. ASSUMED starting implementation: 1 microfarad input and 1 microfarad output ceramic capacitors, nominal rating at least 10 V, accessible package at least 0603. Verify exact-device guidance, effective capacitance with DC bias/tolerance, leakage, inrush, source interaction, and transient behavior before adoption.
  - Rationale: Nominal capacitance values do not alone establish inrush or decoupling suitability.
- **power.reverse_feed**: ASSUMED operating restriction: outputs are loads only; do not externally drive either protected output or parallel it with another supply. Reverse-current blocking is not specified or claimed.
  - Rationale: The candidate high-side switch must not be assumed to provide an unverified reverse-power function.

## Mechanical and manufacturing requirements

- **mechanical.stackup**: REQUIRED: two copper layers, 1 oz copper, nominal 1.6 mm FR-4. No enclosure or mandatory mounting-hole pattern. ASSUMED initial prototype has no mounting holes; retain only if connector fit and practical handling remain acceptable.
  - Rationale: The board is an unenclosed prototype and should not acquire invented enclosure constraints.
- **manufacturing.manual_assembly**: REQUIRED: parts and connectors must be suitable for manual assembly; use accessible SOIC or leaded IC packages and passive sizes at least 0603. No BGA and no IC with an inaccessible underside thermal or ground pad. Explicitly note the USB connector exposed fine-pitch row as an assembly risk; manufacturer documentation does not certify hand soldering.
  - Rationale: Local library availability cannot replace an assessment of solder-joint access and assembly difficulty.
- **libraries.identity_and_mapping**: REQUIRED: use exact locally installed KiCad symbols, real pin numbers, and exact installed footprints. Before wiring, confirm actual symbol pins with project tools; before part-selection completion check every footprint and part-to-footprint correspondence. Check connector geometry, pad mapping, ratings, board-edge placement, access, and mechanical fit separately. Library presence alone establishes none of those suitability claims.
  - Rationale: A drawable symbol and a resolvable footprint can still describe the wrong physical/electrical part.
- **environment.prototype_defaults**: ASSUMED environment: dry indoor bench use, 0 to 50 degrees C ambient, no enclosure, no conformal coating, and normal ESD-controlled handling. Component bounds and later thermal tests must cover that ambient range; no environmental, EMC, ESD-immunity, or regulatory qualification is claimed.
  - Rationale: A stated provisional environment makes current and thermal worst-case checks meaningful without inventing certification.

## Candidate research and its limitations

- **candidate.mic2544_identity**: SUPPLIED RESEARCH, not independently verified here: candidate MIC2544-2YM; reported local symbol Power_Management:MIC2544-2YM and footprint Package_SO:SOIC-8_3.9x4.9mm_P1.27mm. Reported SOIC pins: 1 EN active-low, 2 FLG open-drain, 3 GND, 4 ILIM, 5 NC, 6 OUT, 7 IN, 8 OUT. Both OUT pins must connect if confirmed. Verify exact variant and actual library pins before assigning nets.
  - Rationale: The supplied pin map is a research lead rather than tool-verified wiring authority.
- **candidate.mic2544_voltage_faults**: SUPPLIED RESEARCH [E1,E2]: MIC2544-family operating VIN is 2.7-5.5 V; 7 V absolute maximum is a stress limit. Reported fault behavior is current limiting/foldback and thermal cycling rather than latching. Verify exact-variant behavior, conditions, and recovery before final selection; sustained shorts can cause repeated thermal cycling and heating. No bench safety result exists.
  - Rationale: A current limiter is not a precise 500 mA entitlement controller or proof of safe indefinite fault operation.
- **candidate.current_limit_setting**: SUPPLIED starting candidate: 301 ohm 1% RSET. Using supplied factor bounds 161-299 V and RSET tolerance gives 161/(301*1.01) = approximately 0.530 A and 299/(301*0.99) = approximately 1.003 A; supplied typical estimate is approximately 0.764 A. These estimates are not verified guaranteed limits over all project conditions. Confirm formula, device option, voltage/temperature/test scope, programming current, and tolerance before acceptance. Do not choose a nominal 500 mA setting that can limit below the required 500 mA external load plus protected-rail LED demand. Size the circuit and test faults against the credible upper current, not just the normal load.
  - Rationale: Normal load capability and the wider protection threshold are different constraints.
- **candidate.conduction_loss**: SUPPLIED RESEARCH: enabled supply current up to 160 microampere and on-resistance up to 120 milliohm at the stated 5 V / 500 mA test point. For exactly 500 mA switch current, I^2R estimates 30 mW conduction loss and IR estimates 60 mV drop; actual switch current also includes the protected LED. These are calculations at the cited point, not measurements, not fault dissipation, and not guarantees at every condition.
  - Rationale: Thermal cycling during a short cannot be justified by a normal-load I^2R calculation.
- **candidate.usb_connector**: SUPPLIED candidate: GCT USB4105-GF-A; footprint candidate Connector_USB:USB_C_Receptacle_GCT_USB4105-xx-A_16P_TopMnt_Horizontal. Manufacturer research [E4,E5] reports 5 A COMBINED across VBUS contacts and 48 V DC rated voltage, not 5 A per contact. Verify exact local mapping and mechanical fit; neither ratings nor library presence certify board performance or manual assembly.
  - Rationale: Contact-rating aggregation and exact mechanical identity matter even at the lower normal-load target.
- **cost.supplied_price_provenance**: SUPPLIED distributor observations collected 2026-10-08: MIC2544-2YM quantity-100 unit price USD 0.83 [E3]; USB4105-GF-A quantity-100 unit price USD 0.5745 [E6]. These are dated observations, not live availability checks, delivered-price guarantees, or a complete component BOM. All other fitted parts need itemized dated evidence or labeled uncertain estimates.
  - Rationale: The cost target must not be certified from two incomplete price snapshots.

## Verification, evidence, and firmware applicability

- **firmware.applicability**: REQUIRED: no programmable device and no onboard firmware. Specification-level applicability conclusion: onboard firmware is NOT APPLICABLE because this device is a passive interconnect/indicator plus analog active-protection circuit with no programmable component permitted. This is requirements evidence, not an as-built BOM audit. Reconfirm the conclusion against the actual selected BOM and schematic later. Preserve the real firmware-stage result, including any pipeline blocker; never invent a build, meaningless source file, or unrelated MCU/software to satisfy a file-existence check. MCU strapping-pin and RTC-capability checks are inapplicable only while the no-MCU requirement is maintained.
  - Rationale: Applicability is a documented conclusion, not permission to silently remove a pipeline stage.
- **evidence.prototype_status**: REQUIRED truthful status: no prototype has been manufactured or physically tested. Physical electrical, short-circuit, recovery, thermal, visibility, and assembly validation remain outstanding and belong in the bring-up plan. A finished software draft is not a manufacturing or bench-qualification certificate.
  - Rationale: Design calculations and software checks cannot stand in for physical results.
- **pipeline.deliverables_and_gates**: REQUIRED: preserve all eight original Copperhead stages and their proposal, verification, artifact, and commit gates. Produce specification, architecture, itemized BOM, a non-empty schematic, initial PCB, fabrication/render exports, and bring-up/development plan through the actual pipeline. Use original ERC, DRC, drift, pin/symbol/footprint, and legibility checks where applicable; read and reconcile reports rather than claim guessed passes. Clearly label draft layout and all remaining unrouted connections. Stage 1 creates requirements only and does not claim downstream stage completion.
  - Rationale: The independent test exercises the normal pipeline without replacing its real outcomes.
- **validation.bringup_scope**: REQUIRED later bring-up plan: verify connector polarity and assembly, CC1/CC2 separation and both plug orientations, known-capable source/cable operation, unloaded input current at operating extremes, 500 mA total external load on each connector alone and shared, LED visibility, voltage drop, startup/inrush, overload/current-limit spread, sustained short heating/thermal cycling, and recovery after fault removal. Test the common protection path for both outputs and LED. Record real conditions, equipment, results, and remaining uncertainties; do not mark any physical test passed before execution.
  - Rationale: The plan must address the risks that library and schematic checks cannot resolve.

## Supplied source references

These links and the observations attributed to them were supplied in the brief; listing them does not mean this stage fetched or verified them.

- E1: Microchip official datasheet, https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/DeviceDoc/20005725B.pdf
- E2: Microchip current-family document, https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/APID/ProductDocuments/DataSheets/MIC2544-48-Programmable-Current-Limit-High-Side-Switch-DS20005725.pdf
- E3: MIC2544-2YM distributor snapshot, collected 2026-10-08, https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/microchip-technology/MIC2544-2YM/1028564
- E4: GCT connector specification, https://gct.co/files/specs/usb4105-spec.pdf
- E5: GCT connector drawing, https://gct.co/files/drawings/usb4105.pdf
- E6: USB4105-GF-A distributor snapshot, collected 2026-10-08, https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/gct/USB4105-GF-A/11198441

## Open questions and next-stage acceptance

- Confirm exact MIC2544-2YM pins, enable polarity, current-limit equation/test bounds, fault recovery, and the supply-current definition, especially ILIM current. The 1 mA programming allocation is unproven; it is not permission to ignore a larger actual contribution.
- Close every unloaded-current bin using non-overlapping worst-case evidence. Reject or replace any candidate that cannot preserve strictly below 2 mA while delivering the full external-load requirement. Current-budget compliance is presently UNKNOWN.
- Select exact LED, capacitors, resistors, screw terminal, and header; verify ratings, package accessibility, connector orientation, installed symbols/footprints, and mechanical correspondence. Add any additional protective parts to both cost and leakage accounting.
- Build the itemized quantity-100 BOM and refresh evidence as needed. Cost-target compliance is presently UNKNOWN.
- Develop the original downstream artifacts and perform applicable software checks. Preserve actual firmware-stage applicability/blocker reporting. Leave all physical tests explicitly pending until a prototype is assembled and tested.

# USB-C power input

## Requirements
The board SHALL accept nominal 5 V, 4.75-5.25 V sink-side VBUS with no USB data, USB-PD negotiation, or voltage conversion. CC1 and CC2 SHALL each have their own 5.1 kohm Rd to GND and SHALL NOT be joined. ASSUMED Rd tolerance is 1%. Full-load use requires a known-capable source and cable accounting for board overhead and startup demand; Rd does not negotiate current entitlement or enforce advertised current.

### Scenario: Attachment in either orientation
- Given a suitable source and cable and the input within 4.75-5.25 V
- When either USB-C plug orientation is used
- Then each CC pin has its own Rd path and the board can attach without connecting CC1 to CC2 or claiming USB-PD negotiation.

### Scenario: Full-load operating condition
- Given a proposed 500 mA external load
- When assessing the source and cable
- Then their capability must account for the external load, board overhead, and startup demand; Rd alone is not evidence of entitlement.

### Scenario: Outside the specified range
- Given a 6 V input or another out-of-range condition
- When reviewing suitability
- Then the design makes no operating or sustained-short guarantee based on a 7 V absolute-maximum stress rating.

Rationale: attachment, allowable load, and component stress ratings are separate facts. Source of truth: docs/SPEC.md.

# Common protected outputs

## Requirements
An active high-side protection block SHALL precede both parallel outputs and the LED. The total normal continuous external load SHALL reach 500 mA with either output used alone or with that total shared; internal consumption is additional. Outputs SHALL be one 2-pin 3.5 mm screw terminal and one 2x2 2.54 mm header. A passive fuse alone SHALL NOT substitute for active protection.

ASSUMED pin proposal, pending real-part mapping: screw terminal 1 = +5V_PROTECTED and 2 = GND; header 1/3 = +5V_PROTECTED and 2/4 = GND. Mark polarity and pin 1 and document actual orientation. ASSUMED outputs only drive loads and are not externally powered; no reverse-current-blocking guarantee is made. ASSUMED output tracks input minus circuit losses, without regulation.

MIC2544-2YM, the supplied pin map, 301 ohm 1% RSET, and 1 microfarad input/output capacitors are provisional. Supplied current-limit estimates are approximately 0.530-1.003 A with a typical 0.764 A; confirm all conditions and include LED demand. Supplied fault research describes limiting/foldback and thermal cycling, not latching or verified safe indefinite shorts. See docs/SPEC.md for exact evidence provenance, control proposal, current accounting, and capacitor assumptions.

### Scenario: Shared normal load
- Given verified source/cable capability and verified component suitability
- When either output alone draws 500 mA or both outputs share a 500 mA total
- Then both output paths use the common protected rail and the chosen threshold must not limit below the required external load plus protected-rail LED current.

### Scenario: Fault and recovery review
- Given an overload or short on either output
- When documenting expected protection and recovery
- Then use exact-device evidence for limiting/foldback and thermal behavior, account for effects on both outputs and LED, and leave physical fault/thermal/recovery results pending until measured.

### Scenario: Wiring approval
- Given candidate symbol and footprint identifiers
- When assigning connector or switch nets
- Then verify actual library pin numbers, variant polarity, both OUT pins, pad mapping, and drawings before adopting the proposed assignments.

Rationale: one protection domain and explicit physical mapping prevent bypass paths and false safety claims.

# Protected power indication and unloaded consumption

## Requirements
A visible LED SHALL be on +5V_PROTECTED. Total steady-state unloaded VBUS input current SHALL be strictly below 2 mA throughout 4.75-5.25 V and the ASSUMED 0-50 degrees C ambient range, accounting for tolerances. Both external outputs are open, the switch is enabled and settled, and there is no fault or backfeed. CC-source current is separate from VBUS input current.

ASSUMED provisional allocations in mA: LED 0.531; enabled switch supply/control 0.160; ILIM/control current excluded from that definition 1.000; absent external pull-ups 0; capacitor leakage 0.050; PCB/connector/other fitted protection leakage 0.050; other unplanned loads 0. Allocation sum 1.791, leaving 0.209 to the exclusive 2 mA boundary. This is NOT a verified worst-case sum. Several actual bounds and the supply-current inclusion boundary are UNKNOWN. Count each physical contribution once only. Reallocate only with documentation while preserving the strict whole-board target.

ASSUMED LED candidate: efficient red LED and 10 kohm 1% resistor. The conservative 5.25 V / 9900 ohm calculation is 0.530304 mA, rounded to 0.531 mA, with no invented Vf minimum. Visibility is unverified. The 0.160 mA switch figure is supplied research with unverified conditions; the 1.000 mA programming allowance is an assumption, not datasheet evidence.

### Scenario: Worst-case current closure
- Given the final fitted-parts inventory and applicable device data
- When constructing the unloaded-current sum
- Then every VBUS-fed current and leakage path has a justified worst-case bound, non-overlapping accounting, and a total strictly below 2 mA; a nominal or incomplete sum is insufficient.

### Scenario: Missing programming-current evidence
- Given an unresolved ILIM-current bound or unclear inclusion in supply current
- When evaluating the candidate
- Then report the total as UNKNOWN rather than treating the allocation as proven or counting the same current twice.

### Scenario: Power indication
- Given the minimum allowed input and proposed LED/resistor
- When the protected rail is active
- Then verify visible indication in the expected viewing conditions; a current-limit calculation alone does not establish brightness.

Rationale: all planned and unplanned consumers compete for one strict input-current budget. Source of truth: docs/SPEC.md.

# Manufacturable prototype and component cost

## Requirements
The target board SHALL be no larger than 40 x 30 mm with two copper layers, 1 oz copper, and nominal 1.6 mm FR-4. ASSUMED initial outline is rectangular 40 x 30 mm without mounting holes; there is no enclosure or mandatory hole pattern. Parts SHALL support manual assembly, use accessible SOIC/leaded IC packages and passives at least 0603, and avoid BGA and inaccessible underside IC pads. The USB connector fine-pitch exposed row remains an explicit assembly risk.

The fitted component BOM target SHALL be strictly below USD 8 per board at quantity 100, including every connector and support part, excluding PCB fabrication, assembly, shipping, and tax. Use dated evidence or labeled uncertain estimates. The supplied 2026-10-08 USD 0.83 MIC2544-2YM and USD 0.5745 USB4105-GF-A observations are incomplete snapshots, not current availability or delivered-price guarantees.

ASSUMED environment is dry indoor bench use, 0-50 degrees C ambient, no enclosure/coating, with ESD-controlled handling; no qualification is claimed. Exact installed KiCad identities are required, but installation alone does not establish electrical, physical, or assembly suitability. Candidate USB4105 ratings are 5 A combined over VBUS contacts and 48 V DC according to supplied research, not 5 A per contact.

### Scenario: Part-selection review
- Given an exact proposed MPN, symbol, and footprint
- When accepting the part for the BOM
- Then verify installed identities, actual pins, pad mapping, ratings, package access, and mechanical fit separately.

### Scenario: Cost review
- Given the complete fitted component list
- When evaluating the quantity-100 target
- Then count all fitted parts and disclose dated or uncertain pricing; two candidate price snapshots alone cannot establish the total.

### Scenario: Assembly review
- Given the board and selected connectors
- When assessing manual assembly
- Then check solder-joint access, connector fit, polarity marking, and fine-pitch USB risk rather than claim the manufacturer certified hand soldering.

Rationale: component availability, electrical suitability, assembly practicality, and price evidence require separate checks. Source of truth: docs/SPEC.md.

# Evidence, pipeline integrity, and firmware applicability

## Requirements
All eight original pipeline stages and their proposal, verification, artifact, and commit gates SHALL be preserved. Required deliverables are specification, architecture, itemized BOM, non-empty schematic, initial PCB, fabrication/render exports, and bring-up/development plan. Run applicable original ERC, DRC, drift, symbol/pin/footprint, and legibility checks and reconcile actual reports. Label draft layout and remaining unrouted connections honestly.

The board SHALL contain no programmable device or onboard firmware. The specification-level firmware applicability conclusion is NOT APPLICABLE because programmable devices are forbidden; confirm later against the real BOM and schematic. Preserve the firmware stage's real result or blocker; do not delete the stage, add dummy code, or invent a build. MCU strapping and RTC checks are inapplicable only while there is no MCU.

No prototype has been manufactured or physically tested. Physical validation remains pending. Later bring-up must address assembly/polarity, both USB orientations and separated CC termination, source capability, worst-case unloaded current, 500 mA external load individually/shared, LED visibility, voltage drop, inrush, overload/current-limit behavior, sustained-short thermal cycling, and recovery. Supply actual test conditions and results only after execution.

### Scenario: Firmware-stage execution
- Given a BOM and schematic containing no programmable device as required
- When the original firmware stage runs
- Then record its genuine applicability outcome and evidence, or its real blocker, without fabricated source or build output.

### Scenario: Draft delivery
- Given software-generated design artifacts and verification reports
- When presenting completion of a stage
- Then distinguish achieved software checks from pending downstream gates and physical validation; do not call the draft bench-qualified or ready for manufacture without supporting evidence.

### Scenario: Supplied public research
- Given sources and observations embedded in the original brief
- When citing them
- Then identify them as supplied research rather than independent browsing, local-tool verification, live prices, or measured performance.

Rationale: honest applicability and evidence boundaries are part of the design requirements. Source of truth: docs/SPEC.md.

args.value: REQUIRED: nominal 5 V USB-C VBUS input; guaranteed design operating range must cover 4.75 to 5.25 V. No guaranteed operation or sustained-short performance at 6 V is required.

REQUIRED: deliver up to and including 500 mA TOTAL normal continuous external load across the two parallel outputs; either connector must carry the full 500 mA when used alone. The LED and protection/control currents are additional input demand, not part of that external-load allowance.

REQUIRED: total steady-state unloaded VBUS input current is strictly LESS THAN 2 mA, with both external outputs open and the protection enabled. The numeric boundary 2 is exclusive. Count LED, enabled protection/control, programming and pull-up currents not already included in another entry, all leakage, and every other fitted VBUS-fed load. Demonstrate the worst case throughout 4.75-5.25 V and the ASSUMED ambient range, including component tolerances. Startup and fault current are separate operating cases, not disguised as unloaded steady-state current.

ASSUMED design candidate/allocation: a protected-rail LED with a 10 kohm, 1% series resistor has a conservative current ceiling of 0.531 mA at 5.25 V, using Rmin = 9900 ohm and the deliberately conservative bound Vf >= 0 V: 5.25/9900 = 0.530304 mA, rounded upward. No minimum brightness or actual LED Vf has yet been verified.

ASSUMED preliminary allocation: 0.160 mA for enabled switch supply/control current. SUPPLIED RESEARCH reports a 160 microampere maximum for MIC2544-2YM under datasheet conditions; the exact conditions, full operating-range coverage, and inclusion or exclusion of ILIM and other terminal currents remain unverified.

ASSUMED preliminary allocation: at most 1.000 mA of additional VBUS input current for ILIM programming and control paths EXCLUDED from the preceding supply-current definition. The actual upper bound is UNKNOWN. If the datasheet includes a contribution in supply current, count it there only and do not also count it here.

ASSUMED preliminary allocation: 0 mA for external pull-ups because the proposed always-enabled, unmonitored implementation fits no FLG pull-up and no VBUS-fed EN bias resistor. This zero applies only if that topology is confirmed electrically suitable for the exact variant. Any later fitted bias or pull-up must receive its own worst-case current entry.
ASSUMED preliminary allocation: input and output capacitor leakage combined must be at most 0.050 mA at worst-case voltage and temperature. Actual component leakage bounds have not been obtained.

ASSUMED preliminary allocation: at most 0.050 mA combined for connector/PCB insulation leakage and any other fitted VBUS-connected protection-device leakage not already included above. Actual bounds and any added-device list remain unverified.

ASSUMED preliminary allocation: 0 mA for other VBUS-fed loads because none are currently proposed. This is an inventory assumption, not a measured zero. Adding any load requires updating the budget and its constraint record.

ASSUMED allocation sum: 0.531 + 0.160 + 1.000 + 0 + 0.050 + 0.050 + 0 = 1.791 mA, leaving 0.209 mA below the exclusive 2 mA boundary. This is a planning allocation, NOT a verified worst-case device-current sum. The actual worst-case total is UNKNOWN until every contribution has a justified bound and non-overlapping accounting. Reallocations require documentation and must preserve the strictly below 2 mA requirement.

REQUIRED target: fitted component BOM strictly below USD 8 per board at quantity 100, including USB-C input, both output connectors, active protection, LED, and every supporting component; exclude PCB fabrication, assembly, shipping, and tax. The numeric boundary 8 is exclusive. Use dated price evidence or explicitly uncertain estimates. No complete BOM or verified cost total exists at this stage.
REQUIRED target board envelope no larger than 40 x 30 mm. ASSUMED initial rectangular envelope: 40 x 30 mm, subject to exact connector fit and accessible assembly.

REQUIRED: this is a NEW independent protected USB-C 500 mA power-breakout prototype test input, not a revision of the previous 3 A / USD 3 design. It is a sink-side power input with no USB data, no USB-PD negotiation, and no voltage conversion.
forbidden: inheritance of the previous 3 A / USD 3 specification

args.value: REQUIRED: fit separate 5.1 kohm Rd resistors from CC1 to GND and from CC2 to GND; never join CC1 and CC2. ASSUMED resistor tolerance: 1%. Rd enables attachment; it does not negotiate a current entitlement or enforce the source advertised-current limit.

REQUIRED operating condition: full-load use requires a known-capable source and cable suitable for 500 mA external load PLUS board overhead and startup demand. This power-only design does not establish advertised-current entitlement through Rd alone. Source/cable and protection interactions during inrush/overload require validation.

REQUIRED: one 2-pin 3.5 mm screw terminal and one 2x2 2.54 mm header, connected in parallel downstream of common protection. ASSUMED proposed pin assignment: screw terminal pin 1 = +5V_PROTECTED, pin 2 = GND; header pins 1 and 3 = +5V_PROTECTED, pins 2 and 4 = GND. Clearly mark polarity and pin 1 on the board and document the actual view/orientation. Confirm these proposals against actual symbol pins, footprint pad numbers, and the selected connector drawings before wiring.

ASSUMED: output voltage tracks input minus protection, connector, and copper voltage drops; no tighter regulated output-voltage minimum is specified. Calculate worst-case loaded drop at the minimum input and include it in later review.

REQUIRED: a common active high-side short-circuit protection block precedes BOTH external outputs and the visible power LED. A passive fuse is not an acceptable substitute. Explain fault-control and recovery using exact-device evidence; do not claim tested fault safety.
forbidden: LED upstream of common active protection

args.value: ASSUMED candidate implementation: MIC2544-2YM always enabled using its reported active-low EN tied to GND, FLG intentionally unconnected without a pull-up, and NC left unconnected; connect both reported OUT pins. These are proposals pending exact-variant datasheet and actual-library pin confirmation. No MCU is introduced to operate or observe the switch.

REQUIRED: a visible power LED on +5V_PROTECTED. ASSUMED starting choice: efficient red indicator with the budgeted 10 kohm 1% resistor; select its actual part and check visibility at minimum input and expected viewing conditions.

SUPPLIED RESEARCH: input decoupling guidance is 0.1-1 microfarad near the switch. ASSUMED starting implementation: 1 microfarad input and 1 microfarad output ceramic capacitors, nominal rating at least 10 V, accessible package at least 0603. Verify exact-device guidance, effective capacitance with DC bias/tolerance, leakage, inrush, source interaction, and transient behavior before adoption.
ASSUMED operating restriction: outputs are loads only; do not externally drive either protected output or parallel it with another supply. Reverse-current blocking is not specified or claimed.

REQUIRED: two copper layers, 1 oz copper, nominal 1.6 mm FR-4. No enclosure or mandatory mounting-hole pattern. ASSUMED initial prototype has no mounting holes; retain only if connector fit and practical handling remain acceptable.

REQUIRED: parts and connectors must be suitable for manual assembly; use accessible SOIC or leaded IC packages and passive sizes at least 0603. No BGA and no IC with an inaccessible underside thermal or ground pad. Explicitly note the USB connector exposed fine-pitch row as an assembly risk; manufacturer documentation does not certify hand soldering.
forbidden: IC with inaccessible underside thermal/ground pad

args.value: REQUIRED: use exact locally installed KiCad symbols, real pin numbers, and exact installed footprints. Before wiring, confirm actual symbol pins with project tools; before part-selection completion check every footprint and part-to-footprint correspondence. Check connector geometry, pad mapping, ratings, board-edge placement, access, and mechanical fit separately. Library presence alone establishes none of those suitability claims.

ASSUMED environment: dry indoor bench use, 0 to 50 degrees C ambient, no enclosure, no conformal coating, and normal ESD-controlled handling. Component bounds and later thermal tests must cover that ambient range; no environmental, EMC, ESD-immunity, or regulatory qualification is claimed.

SUPPLIED RESEARCH, not independently verified here: candidate MIC2544-2YM; reported local symbol Power_Management:MIC2544-2YM and footprint Package_SO:SOIC-8_3.9x4.9mm_P1.27mm. Reported SOIC pins: 1 EN active-low, 2 FLG open-drain, 3 GND, 4 ILIM, 5 NC, 6 OUT, 7 IN, 8 OUT. Both OUT pins must connect if confirmed. Verify exact variant and actual library pins before assigning nets.

SUPPLIED RESEARCH [E1,E2]: MIC2544-family operating VIN is 2.7-5.5 V; 7 V absolute maximum is a stress limit. Reported fault behavior is current limiting/foldback and thermal cycling rather than latching. Verify exact-variant behavior, conditions, and recovery before final selection; sustained shorts can cause repeated thermal cycling and heating. No bench safety result exists.

SUPPLIED starting candidate: 301 ohm 1% RSET. Using supplied factor bounds 161-299 V and RSET tolerance gives 161/(301*1.01) = approximately 0.530 A and 299/(301*0.99) = approximately 1.003 A; supplied typical estimate is approximately 0.764 A. These estimates are not verified guaranteed limits over all project conditions. Confirm formula, device option, voltage/temperature/test scope, programming current, and tolerance before acceptance. Do not choose a nominal 500 mA setting that can limit below the required 500 mA external load plus protected-rail LED demand. Size the circuit and test faults against the credible upper current, not just the normal load.

SUPPLIED RESEARCH: enabled supply current up to 160 microampere and on-resistance up to 120 milliohm at the stated 5 V / 500 mA test point. For exactly 500 mA switch current, I^2R estimates 30 mW conduction loss and IR estimates 60 mV drop; actual switch current also includes the protected LED. These are calculations at the cited point, not measurements, not fault dissipation, and not guarantees at every condition.

SUPPLIED candidate: GCT USB4105-GF-A; footprint candidate Connector_USB:USB_C_Receptacle_GCT_USB4105-xx-A_16P_TopMnt_Horizontal. Manufacturer research [E4,E5] reports 5 A COMBINED across VBUS contacts and 48 V DC rated voltage, not 5 A per contact. Verify exact local mapping and mechanical fit; neither ratings nor library presence certify board performance or manual assembly.

SUPPLIED distributor observations collected 2026-10-08: MIC2544-2YM quantity-100 unit price USD 0.83 [E3]; USB4105-GF-A quantity-100 unit price USD 0.5745 [E6]. These are dated observations, not live availability checks, delivered-price guarantees, or a complete component BOM. All other fitted parts need itemized dated evidence or labeled uncertain estimates.

REQUIRED: no programmable device and no onboard firmware. Specification-level applicability conclusion: onboard firmware is NOT APPLICABLE because this device is a passive interconnect/indicator plus analog active-protection circuit with no programmable component permitted. This is requirements evidence, not an as-built BOM audit. Reconfirm the conclusion against the actual selected BOM and schematic later. Preserve the real firmware-stage result, including any pipeline blocker; never invent a build, meaningless source file, or unrelated MCU/software to satisfy a file-existence check. MCU strapping-pin and RTC-capability checks are inapplicable only while the no-MCU requirement is maintained.

REQUIRED truthful status: no prototype has been manufactured or physically tested. Physical electrical, short-circuit, recovery, thermal, visibility, and assembly validation remain outstanding and belong in the bring-up plan. A finished software draft is not a manufacturing or bench-qualification certificate.

REQUIRED: preserve all eight original Copperhead stages and their proposal, verification, artifact, and commit gates. Produce specification, architecture, itemized BOM, a non-empty schematic, initial PCB, fabrication/render exports, and bring-up/development plan through the actual pipeline. Use original ERC, DRC, drift, pin/symbol/footprint, and legibility checks where applicable; read and reconcile reports rather than claim guessed passes. Clearly label draft layout and all remaining unrouted connections. Stage 1 creates requirements only and does not claim downstream stage completion.

REQUIRED later bring-up plan: verify connector polarity and assembly, CC1/CC2 separation and both plug orientations, known-capable source/cable operation, unloaded input current at operating extremes, 500 mA total external load on each connector alone and shared, LED visibility, voltage drop, startup/inrush, overload/current-limit spread, sustained short heating/thermal cycling, and recovery after fault removal. Test the common protection path for both outputs and LED. Record real conditions, equipment, results, and remaining uncertainties; do not mark any physical test passed before execution.

args.decision: Keep this specification independent of the previous 3 A / USD 3 breakout and retain the original eight-stage pipeline.
args.rationale: The new 500 mA brief has its own budgets and requires genuine downstream gate outcomes.

args.decision: Use a complete but explicitly unclosed current-accounting framework with a provisional 1.791 mA allocation, including a 1.000 mA unresolved programming/control bin.
args.rationale: The strictly below 2 mA target cannot be certified from supplied nominal or condition-limited values; resolve current-definition overlap before summing real currents.

args.decision: Retain MIC2544-2YM, 301 ohm 1% RSET, USB4105-GF-A, and decoupling values as candidates pending actual-device and local-library verification.
args.rationale: Supplied research and library identity do not establish current-budget, fault, pin, package, or mechanical suitability.

args.decision: Propose always-enabled protection without an external FLG pull-up or unused EN bias network; keep NC unconnected if exact-device verification confirms the reported pins.
args.rationale: An unobserved status output and permanently active protection do not justify additional standing current; these intentional absences remain provisional until exact-variant validation.

args.decision: Propose terminal 1 positive/2 ground and header 1/3 positive, 2/4 ground, plus explicit pin-1/polarity markings, subject to real-part mapping.
args.rationale: A documented repeated power/ground pair reduces wiring ambiguity without pretending the candidate footprint orientation has been checked.

args.decision: Record onboard firmware as not applicable at requirements level and preserve the real firmware-stage result or blocker.
args.rationale: The brief forbids programmable hardware and dummy software; final applicability still needs the selected BOM and schematic as evidence.

args.decision: Leave all physical validation pending and distinguish supplied research, calculations, assumptions, and actual software verification.
args.rationale: No prototype has been manufactured or bench-tested, and a reviewable draft cannot certify fault safety or manufacturing qualification.
